sentences.text: This small theropod dinosaur reached an estimated total length of 2.4 metres and weighed between 12 and 21.8 kilograms.

Distinctive anatomical features include the base of the ilion being half the diameter of the hip joint, an accessory trochanter on the femur, and a tibial joint interior that is significantly enlarged.
He Xinlu described Chuandongocoelurus in 1984 from remains found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation, initially classifying it as a coelurosaurian.

The holotype specimen for Chuandongocoelurus primitivus is a thighbone catalogued as CCG 20010, measuring 201 millimetres in length, which had unfused neurocentral sutures indicating the animal was immature when it died.
The tibia of the holotype measures 231 millimetres in length.
Chuandongocoelurus was originally classified within Coeluridae, a group at the time used as a catch-all for almost all small theropods.
In 1990, David Bruce Norman considered Chuandongocoelurus to be an indeterminate theropod.

Research by Roger Benson and colleagues suggests Chuandongocoelurus is the sister taxon of Monolophosaurus, forming a clade that may belong to Megalosauroidea or lie outside it within Tetanurae, while a 2012 study by Matthew Carrano and colleagues placed Chuandongocoelurus outside the Megalosauroidea group.
Chuandongocoelurus lived approximately 165 to 161 million years ago during the Bathonian and Callovian stages of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Asia.
In 2012, researchers concluded that the two specimens originally assigned to Chuandongocoelurus represent different taxa that are likely not closely related.
